feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: U.S. military destroys 5 Iranian oil tankers as back-and-forth strikes continue
entry.summary: The U.S. military destroyed five Iranian oil tankers Tuesday and Iran struck back, targeting U.S. troops in Jordan.

entry.title: Retired General Joseph Votel discusses Iran's latest attacks
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with retired General Joseph Votel about the latest attacks and counterattacks from Iran.

entry.title: Missouri's redistricting fight in turmoil after two different federal court decisions
entry.summary: The redistricting that Republicans hoped would help them win a key House seat in Missouri is in limbo after contradictory court rulings.

entry.title: Citing the 'Deep State,' Trump overhauls the intelligence community
entry.summary: The catastrophic 9/11 attacks forced the intelligence community to radically revamp its ways of doing business. Now, critics say, President Trump is dismantling much of what was built since then.

entry.title: Ballot seizures seemed impossible. But judges and officials are prepping for them now
entry.summary: The idea of law enforcement taking possession of ballots in the middle of an active election used to be considered impossible. Now, it's a scenario voting officials — and judges — are training for.

entry.title: Trump promises $5,000 dividend in convention speech, but only if Republicans win
entry.summary: Calling it a "Trump dividend," the president announced a $5,000 payment for every adult citizen if the Republican Party maintains control of the House and Senate in the midterm election.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Back-and-forth strikes between the U.S. and Iran continue, U.K. imposes sanctions on Israeli settlements, accusing settlers of "ethnic cleansing," Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie G. Bunch III resigns.

entry.title: Colin Kaepernick reflects on Jay-Z 'disappointing' him, losing the NFL and finding his power
entry.summary: A decade after taking a knee, Colin Kaepernick has no regrets and is reflecting on his life in his new memoir, The Perilous Fight. He talks to NPR's Michel Martin about losing football, his disappointment with Jay-Z and what the protest taught him about power.

entry.title: New York City Mayor Mamdani releases documents related to post-9/11 air quality
entry.summary: New York City has released 170,000 documents it says show officials knew the air quality around the World Trade Center after 9/11 was dangerous to breathe, but they didn't warn local residents.

entry.title: Oregon nonprofit harvests fruit from backyards and parks for people in need
entry.summary: In the Portland, Oregon, area, a nonprofit harvests edible fruit from thousands of metro trees, shrubs and bushes, and distributes it to people in need.
